solutions.name: Manual workaround
solutions.category: Spreadsheet, notes, or ad hoc process
solutions.observed_positioning: Cheap and flexible, but slow and inconsistent.

solutions.name: Generic horizontal SaaS
solutions.observed_positioning: Easy to adopt, but weak on domain-specific outcomes.

solutions.name: Incumbent enterprise platform
solutions.observed_positioning: Trusted by buyers, but expensive and slow to implement.

solutions.name: Internal build
solutions.observed_positioning: Fits local process, but competes with engineering priorities.

solutions.name: Consulting or agency service
solutions.observed_positioning: High-touch expertise, but margins and scale are limited.

solutions.name: Open-source project
solutions.observed_positioning: Low software cost, but support and reliability vary.

solutions.name: AI wrapper
solutions.observed_positioning: Fast to build, but easy to copy if workflow depth is missing.

solutions.name: Marketplace or network
solutions.observed_positioning: Useful when liquidity exists, hard to start from zero.

solutions.name: Mobile-first app
solutions.observed_positioning: Good distribution surface, often too shallow for serious workflows.

solutions.name: No-code automation
solutions.observed_positioning: Good for prototypes, brittle for core operations.

solutions.name: Legacy desktop software
solutions.category: Installed tool or old vertical app
solutions.observed_positioning: Embedded in workflows, poor UX and integrations.

solutions.name: Data dashboard
solutions.observed_positioning: Makes status visible, but may not drive action.

solutions.name: Community and content
solutions.observed_positioning: Can validate demand, but may not be software defensible.

solutions.name: API infrastructure
solutions.observed_positioning: Scales well if developers are the buyer, indirect otherwise.

solutions.name: Status quo
solutions.observed_positioning: Always a competitor when pain is tolerable or budget is unclear.

research_summary: Fallback mode cannot perform live market research, so it maps the idea against the common alternative categories every startup must beat: manual work, internal builds, incumbents, consultants, generic SaaS, open-source, and doing nothing.
